task_instance: Following the skill's Worker Pool pattern (Pattern 1), implement a concurrent Go worker pool program that fans 50 jobs out to 5 goroutine workers, propagates context cancellation in both the job-receive and result-send selects, and closes the results channel exactly once from a dedicated sender goroutine after all workers finish; then build/run it and race-test it to confirm it is correct (all 50 jobs processed once, no deadlock, no goroutine leak, no data race).
blocker_detail: The core deliverable of this skill is correct, running concurrent Go code. I could author the program as a text file, but the office-assistant runtime cannot run code of any kind: there is no Go toolchain and no shell, so I cannot compile it (go build), run it (go run), or race-test it (go test -race / the race detector the skill's own Race Detection section prescribes). Correctness of concurrency code (no deadlock, no goroutine leak, no data race, every job processed exactly once) can only be established by execution and the race detector, which are unavailable. Writing text verifies nothing about concurrent behavior, so the deliverable cannot be produced-and-verified in this runtime.
evidence: Read the skill at the skills-repo path plugins/systems-programming/skills/go-concurrency-patterns/SKILL.md and its references/details.md (seven patterns incl. Worker Pool; a Race Detection section instructing go test -race / go run -race). Authored the worker-pool program at the work directory file worker_pool.go (context cancellation in both selects, single sender-side close of results, 5 workers over 50 buffered jobs, deterministic sorted output of processed results; also corrected the skill reference bug where the Result literal used an unresolvable placeholder for JobID by returning job.ID).
